subject.title: [codex] fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup

question: Should `sessions cleanup --enforce` physically remove stale `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archive files according to the existing retention rules and report that in dry-run/apply output?
rationale: The code path is a narrow, tested reuse of the existing archive-retention helper, but it intentionally affects retained session artifacts and intersects broader archive/no-delete policy that automation should not accept on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Accept archive-retention cleanup
options.body: Land the PR if maintainers accept removing stale deleted/reset archives under the existing retention rules and the provided CLI proof.

options.title: Ask for broader upgrade proof
options.body: Pause for a larger real-store or upgrade-style run if maintainers want more confidence before changing operator cleanup behavior.

options.title: Defer to retention policy work
options.body: Hold or close this PR if maintainers want to settle the broader no-delete/archive naming policy before changing cleanup behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept archive-retention cleanup
recommendation.body: Land the PR if maintainers accept removing stale deleted/reset archives under the existing retention rules and the provided CLI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the sessions cleanup command and maintenance controls that this PR changes at the command/operator boundary.
